newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian court grants ex-Nazi Priebke house arrest.
newsitem.headline: Italian court grants ex-Nazi Priebke house arrest.

text.p: An Italian military court granted house arrest on Tuesday to former SS captain Erich Priebke, pending a re-trial for his role in Italy's worst World War Two atrocity, military prosecutor Antonino Intelisano said.

Priebke, 83, has been held in jail since his extradition to Italy from Argentina in November 1995 on charges of complicity in the SS massacre of 335 men and boys, 75 of them Jews, at the Ardeatine Caves south of Rome in March 1944.

His lawyer, Carlo Taormina, told Reuters earlier that he had asked a military court to release his client into house arrest on grounds of deteriorating mental health. Judicial sources have said Priebke could be moved to a Catholic convent or monastery.
Priebke has admitted taking part in the 1944 killings but has argued that he had to follow orders or would have been shot.

He has already been tried once for the crime by an Italian military court. Its verdict that he was guilty but should be allowed to go free caused outrage and was quashed in October on appeal. The re-trial is expected to start next month.
